1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands (unread inbox for your task, your session's runtime/tokens, other live
34	runs) — read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone.
35	
36	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
37	
38	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
39	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
40	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
41	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
42	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
43	
44	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
45	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
46	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
47	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
48	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
49	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
50	
51	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
52	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
53	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
54	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
55	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
56	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
57	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
58	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
59	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
60	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
61	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
62	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
63	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
64	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
65	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
66	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
67	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
68	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
69	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
70	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
71	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
72	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
73	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
74	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
75	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
76	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
77	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
78	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
79	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
80	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
81	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
82	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
83	
84	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
85	
86	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
87	
88	| Variable | Meaning |
89	|---|---|
90	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
91	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
92	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
93	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
94	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
95	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
96	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
97	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
98	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
99	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
100	
101	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
102	
103	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
104	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
105	
106	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
107	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
108	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
109	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
110	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
111	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
112	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
113	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
114	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
115	
116	## One-shot discipline (important)
117	
118	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
119	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
120	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
121	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
122	
123	## Pick the highest-value work
124	
125	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
126	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
127	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
128	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
129	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
130	
131	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
132	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
133	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
134	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
135	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
136	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
137	(it returns to the queue).
138	
139	## Fresh-context checkpoints
140	
141	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
142	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
143	checkpoints:
144	
145	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
146	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
147	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
148	  clean/build result.
149	
150	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
151	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
152	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
153	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
154	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
155	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
156	terminal `done` claim.
157	
158	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
159	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
160	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
161	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
162	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
163	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
164	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
165	
166	## Warnings are work
167	
168	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
169	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
170	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
171	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
172	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
173	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
174	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
175	why.
176	
177	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
178	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
179	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
180	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
181	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
182	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
183	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
184	
185	### Two CLI traps that produce silent or fake warnings
186	
187	Both were paid for the hard way; neither is discoverable from `--help`.
188	
189	- **`task set --status` writes through to the roadmap.** Giving a task a terminal
190	  status (`done`/`cancelled`/…) also rewrites every roadmap item in that task's
191	  `roadmap_refs`, with no mention of it in the output — retiring a duplicate
192	  *task* can flip a live critical-path *milestone* to `rejected`. Read the task's
193	  `roadmap_refs` first, then re-assert the milestone status you actually want with
194	  `roadmap set <ref> --status …` and verify with `roadmap list --json`.
195	- **`graph sync` needs `--blueprint` *and* `--lean`.** With only `--blueprint` the
196	  Lean side is empty, so every `\lean{…}` pin reports "not found in Lean sources"
197	  (thousands of bogus warnings, including pins that are certainly fine). Pass both
198	  paths, or don't believe the count.
199	
200	## Do the work (Lean)
201	
202	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
203	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
204	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
205	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
206	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
207	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
208	configured final build covers the same files.
209	
210	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
211	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
212	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
213	mathlib — query it:
214	
215	| You want | Use | Not |
216	|---|---|---|
217	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
218	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
219	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
220	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
221	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
222	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
223	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
224	
225	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
226	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
227	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
228	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
229	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
230	back to grep.
231	
232	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
233	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
234	
235	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
236	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
237	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
238	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
239	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
240	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
241	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
242	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
243	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
244	
245	## Read the other projects
246	
247	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
248	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
249	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
250	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
251	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
252	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
253	
254	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
255	
256	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
257	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
258	needs no permission.
259	
260	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
261	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
262	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
263	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
264	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
265	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
266	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
267	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
268	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
269	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
270	
271	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
272	
273	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
274	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
275	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
276	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
277	
278	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
279	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
280	
281	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
282	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
283	  as **memory**.
284	
285	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
286	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
287	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
288	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
289	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
290	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
291	shorter. This pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
292	
293	## Resuming after an interruption
294	
295	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
296	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
297	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
298	
299	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
300	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
301	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
302	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
303	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
304	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
305	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
306	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
307	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
308	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
309	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
310	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
311	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
312	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
313	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
314	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
315	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
316	
317	## Final report (your last message)
318	
319	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
320	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
321	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
322	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
323	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
324	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
325	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
326	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
327	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
328	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
329	not by itself a reason to stop.
330	
331	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
332	
333	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
334	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
335	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
336	`subagents` skill):
337	
338	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
339	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
340	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
341	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
342	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
343	
344	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

6	Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
7	before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
8	(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
9	immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
10	ago, and their report was written for you.
11	
12	This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
13	the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
14	tenth of the session.
15	
16	## The four signals
17	
18	```bash
19	ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
20	"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
21	"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
22	"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
23	```
24	
25	The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
26	like:
27	
28	```
29	0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
30	0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
31	0003-system
32	0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
33	```
34	
35	For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:
36	
37	- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
38	  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
39	  single most informative bit on disk.
40	- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
41	  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
42	  four minutes ago or last week.
43	
44	## Which situation am I in?
45	
46	Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.
47	
48	**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
49	kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
50	the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
51	transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
52	the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
53	shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
54	transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
55	doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
56	its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.
57	
58	**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
59	that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
60	`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
61	any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
62	it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
63	ledger.
64	
65	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
66	of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
67	almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
68	roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
69	recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
70	tried and rejected.
71	
72	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
73	interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
74	orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
75	stand before proposing work.
76	
77	One caveat about round numbers. `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is 0-based and reliable
78	for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
79	`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
80	check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
81	resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
82	the run's original plan.)
83	
84	## Then, before you start
85	
86	- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
87	  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
88	- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
89	  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
90	  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.
91	- **The inbox is the cross-session thread** — read what past sessions left for
92	  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
93	  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
94	  `horizon-inbox`.
95	
96	Then stop orienting and start working. The point of this pass is to begin from a
97	smarter place than round zero — not to reconstruct everything that ever happened
98	here.

I've completed the work and left the task status unset so it returns to the queue. Final report:

## Summary

Established the project's real axiom frontier as a reproducible artifact, wired the headline theorem to the infrastructure that is supposed to support it, and re-aimed blueprint, roadmap, hgraph and docs at the Milne–Kollár route the Lean tree actually pursues. A fresh-context review caught me overstating my own central result; that correction is committed too.

The substantive finding: "sorry-free" was being claimed on evidence that cannot detect the leak. `#print axioms` on a theorem that *quantifies over* a sorry-bodied gate reports clean axioms, because the caller discharges the hypothesis. `Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible`, `.isSeparated` and `.locallyOfFiniteType` are all clean as stated and all pick up `sorryAx` the moment a call site must synthesise `HasPicScheme`. The probe measures this with `leakProbe_*`/`leakControl_*` pairs — identical conclusions and proof terms, differing only in whether Lean runs `instHasPicScheme`.

## Progress

- `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`: new; 60 declarations, ~12s warm, zero errors. Covers the headline, both sorry-bodied instances, the Picard/Pic⁰/cohomology/Riemann-Roch/Albanese keystones, and both sibling teams' claims.

- `AlgebraicJacobian.lean`: five previously unrooted modules added; project went 164 → 170 reachable of 172.

Verification: `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` green, 8728 jobs, exit 0. Blueprint PDF 616 pages, zero undefined references.

- **I corrected a wrong claim of my own.** I first wrote that four witness fields were "the landed theorems"; `Pic0.smooth` and `Pic0.proper` are themselves `sorry`-bodied, so the witness rests on **five** obligations, not three. My own probe output had already printed this. Fixed in five artifacts.
- **Leaf A is false as stated.** `hasRationalPoint_and_geometricallyIntegral` asserts a `k`-rational point, which a smooth proper geometrically integral curve need not have. It is a deliberate gap marker — but it means the cone below `picardJacobianWitness` currently rests on an inconsistent hypothesis, and the leaf must be *replaced*, never proved. Said so in the docstring and blueprint.

The root roll-up is one step short **by choice**: ajc-gate's `RigidPushforwardFiberChart` and `RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf` compile green but are untracked in the ledger, so rooting them would break a clean checkout. I backed those two imports out and flagged it. Their claim that `RigidPushforwardGate` transitively pulls them is wrong — both sit above it.
2. I-0372's rational-point decision is unmade, and I was instructed not to make it. Both branches are now recorded in five places with neither assumed.

- Split leaf A: only the rational-point half is a decision. Geometric integrality follows via `Smooth ⟹ GeometricallyReduced`, which sibling AJCR proves in mathlib generality — a portable brick, and an upstreaming candidate.

125	    [GrpObj J₂] [IsProper J₂.hom] [Smooth J₂.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₂.hom]

152	/-- A bundled Albanese witness for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve
153	`C`: a candidate group scheme `J` (with proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible
154	structure, smooth of relative dimension `genus C`), and a proof that `J` satisfies
155	the Albanese universal property of Definition `IsAlbanese` for `C` *for every choice
156	of $k$-rational marked point* `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`.
157	
158	Mathematically, the underlying scheme `J` (and its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
159	structure) is intrinsic to `C`; only the universal morphism `C ⟶ J` depends on the
160	choice of marked point `P`. Encoding `isAlbaneseFor` as a `∀ P, IsAlbanese …` field
161	keeps the bundle independent of any specific pointing, which is what
162	`AbelJacobi.Jacobian.ofCurve P` needs in order to project the Albanese morphism for
163	an *arbitrary* input `P`.
164	
165	The smoothness witness is recorded at the specific relative dimension `genus C`,
166	which is the form required by `Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`. -/
167	structure JacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
168	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] where
169	  /-- The candidate Albanese object. -/
170	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
171	  /-- The group-scheme structure on `J`. -/
172	  grpObj : GrpObj J
173	  /-- `J` is proper over `k`. -/
174	  proper : IsProper J.hom
175	  /-- `J` is smooth over `k`. -/
176	  smooth : Smooth J.hom
177	  /-- `J` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
178	  geomIrred : GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom
179	  /-- `J` is smooth of relative dimension `genus C` (so dim `J = genus C`). -/
180	  smoothGenus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) J.hom
181	  /-- The Albanese universal-property data: for every choice of $k$-rational marked
182	  point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`, the scheme `J` together with its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
183	  structure satisfies the Albanese universal property for the pointed curve `(C, P)`. -/
184	  isAlbaneseFor : ∀ (P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C), @IsAlbanese k _ C P J grpObj proper smooth geomIrred

187	/-! ## The three open leaves of the witness
188	
189	`picardJacobianWitness` below is assembled from the landed `Pic⁰_{C/k}` development
190	(`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`) together with the three statements of this section.
191	They are the entire mathematical distance between the current tree and the headline;
192	everything else in the assembly is projection.
193	
194	Each is stated at the exact strength the assembly consumes, so that a proof of the
195	three closes `picardJacobianWitness` with no further work. -/
196	
197	/-- **Leaf A: the hypothesis gap between the challenge statement and `Pic⁰_{C/k}`.**
198	
199	The ambient hypotheses of `Jacobian C` are `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `IsProper`
200	and `GeometricallyIrreducible`. The Picard development runs instead under
201	`GeometricallyIntegral` and `Scheme.HasRationalPoint`, and both extra hypotheses are
202	load-bearing rather than cosmetic:
203	
204	* `GeometricallyIntegral C.hom` follows from the ambient hypotheses by pure geometry —
205	  a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced, and geometrically reduced plus
206	  geometrically irreducible is geometrically integral
207	  (`GeometricallyIntegral.of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible`). The
208	  missing input is the first implication, `Smooth ⟹ GeometricallyReduced`, which
209	  Mathlib `v4.31` does not carry.
210	* `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` does **not** follow: a smooth proper geometrically
211	  integral curve over a field need not have a `k`-rational point (a genus-`0`
212	  conic without rational points, or the standard genus-`2` example over `ℚ`). It is
213	  available over an algebraically closed field only
214	  (`Albanese.hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed`).
215	
216	So this leaf is not one statement but two of very different natures, and the second is
217	where the challenge statement and the tree currently disagree: `Scheme.instHasPicScheme`
218	takes `[HasRationalPoint C]` and is correct to do so, because without a section
219	`Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` need not even be a Zariski sheaf. Kleiman's theorem needs no
220	section because it represents the *étale* sheaf. The two ways to close the gap —
221	étale-sheafify the Picard functor, or carry the rational point as a hypothesis of the
222	headline and prove something weaker than the challenge asks — are a design decision, not
223	a platform limitation.
224	
225	**Read this leaf as a gap marker, not as an obligation to discharge.** Because its
226	second conjunct is false, the statement is not merely unproved but unprovable, so
227	everything downstream of `picardJacobianWitness` currently rests on an inconsistent
228	hypothesis rather than on an open frontier. That is deliberate — it puts the gap where
229	a reader of the headline meets it, instead of leaving it implicit in the Picard
230	hypotheses — but it means this leaf must be **replaced** once the decision above is
231	made, by either a rational-point binder on the Jacobian itself or an étale-sheafified
232	representability input. It must not be "proved". -/
233	theorem hasRationalPoint_and_geometricallyIntegral (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
234	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
235	    GeometricallyIntegral C.hom ∧ Scheme.HasRationalPoint C :=
236	  sorry
237	
238	/-- **Leaf B: the dimension refinement.**
239	
240	The landed `Scheme.Pic0.smooth` gives bare smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` over `k`; the
241	witness field `smoothGenus` needs it at the specific relative dimension `genus C`. The
242	mathematical content is Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11 together with `Scheme.Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`:
243	the tangent space at the identity is `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`, of dimension `genus C` by definition
244	of `genus`, and for a smooth group scheme the relative dimension equals the dimension of
245	that tangent space. -/
246	theorem smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0 (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
247	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
248	    [Scheme.HasPicScheme C] [Scheme.PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
249	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom :=
250	  sorry
251	
252	/-- **Leaf C: the Albanese universal property, over an arbitrary field and every point.**
253	
254	`Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property` proves exactly this statement, but under two
255	restrictions the witness cannot accept: the base field is algebraically closed, and the
256	genus is positive. The witness needs the property over the ambient field `k` and for
257	*every* choice of `k`-rational marked point `P`, including `genus C = 0` (where
258	`Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k` and the content is the classical rigidity statement that every
259	pointed morphism from a genus-`0` curve to an abelian variety is constant).
260	
261	Descending the algebraically-closed case to `k` is the Galois-descent step of the
262	campaign's cluster `G`; the genus-`0` case is Mumford §4 rigidity. -/
263	theorem isAlbanese_pic0 (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
264	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
265	    [Scheme.HasPicScheme C] [Scheme.PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
266	    (grp : GrpObj (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C)) (pr : IsProper (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
267	    (sm : Smooth (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
268	    (gi : GeometricallyIrreducible (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
269	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
270	    @IsAlbanese k _ C P (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C) grp pr sm gi :=
271	  sorry
272	
273	/-- The Albanese witness for a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve `C`,
274	constructed **uniformly in the genus** as the identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` of the
275	Picard scheme of `C`.
276	
277	By the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*`), `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is representable
278	(`Scheme.PicScheme.representable`) and is an abelian variety of dimension `genus C`:
279	its tangent space at the identity is `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` (`Scheme.Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`),
280	giving smoothness of relative dimension `genus C` (`Scheme.Pic0.smooth`), properness
281	(`Scheme.Pic0.proper`), and geometric irreducibility
282	(`Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible`); the Albanese universal property is the
283	Abel–Jacobi factorisation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.AlbaneseUP`.
284	
285	The genus-`0` case is **not** special and needs no separate construction: when
286	`genus C = 0` the tangent space is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
287	automatically, and the universal property degenerates to the (then trivial) statement
288	that every pointed morphism `C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety is constant. The former
289	`genusZeroWitness` / `positiveGenusWitness` genus split — together with its bespoke
290	rigidity / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery — has been
291	removed in favour of this single uniform witness.
292	
293	The construction below is **wired to the Picard development**: the underlying scheme
294	is `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C`, and four of the six witness fields are theorems of
295	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` applied directly. This definition carries no `sorry`
296	of its own, but that is a statement about this file, not a completeness claim: two of
297	those four upstream theorems (`Pic0.smooth`, `Pic0.proper`) are `sorry`-bodied, so
298	the witness depends on five open obligations — those two, plus the three leaves
299	`hasRationalPoint_and_geometricallyIntegral`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0`
300	and `isAlbanese_pic0` above. -/
301	noncomputable def picardJacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
302	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
303	    JacobianWitness C := by
304	  obtain ⟨hgi, hrp⟩ := hasRationalPoint_and_geometricallyIntegral C
305	  haveI := hgi
306	  haveI := hrp
307	  exact
308	    { J := Scheme.Pic0Scheme C
309	      grpObj := (Scheme.Pic0.grpObj C).some
310	      proper := Scheme.Pic0.proper C
311	      smooth := Scheme.Pic0.smooth C
312	      geomIrred := Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible C
313	      smoothGenus := smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0 C
314	      isAlbaneseFor := fun P => isAlbanese_pic0 C _ _ _ _ P }
315	
316	/-- Existence of an Albanese witness for every smooth proper geometrically irreducible
317	curve, uniformly in the genus via the Picard identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
318	(`picardJacobianWitness`). This packages the five protected obligations (`Jacobian`,
319	`instGrpObj`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`, `instIsProper`,
320	`instGeometricallyIrreducible`) into a single existence statement, and records that the
321	Albanese property of the underlying scheme `J` is uniform over every choice of
322	`k`-rational marked point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C` (via the `isAlbaneseFor` field of
323	`JacobianWitness`). -/
324	theorem nonempty_jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
325	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
326	    Nonempty (JacobianWitness C) :=
327	  ⟨picardJacobianWitness C⟩
328	
329	/-- A choice of Albanese witness for `C`, extracted via `Classical.choice`.
330	Used to define `Jacobian C` and to discharge each of the four protected instances
331	on it. -/
332	noncomputable def jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
333	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
334	    JacobianWitness C :=
335	  Classical.choice (nonempty_jacobianWitness C)
336	
337	-- data
338	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`.
339	
340	The Jacobian is the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness for `C` (see
341	`JacobianWitness` and `nonempty_jacobianWitness`), so it is `Pic⁰_{C/k}` for the
342	witness `picardJacobianWitness`, whose remaining content is the three leaves of
343	§"The three open leaves of the witness". The genus-`0`
344	specialisation is implicit in the witness — a smooth proper geometrically
345	irreducible group scheme over `k` of relative dimension `0` is `Spec k` — so
346	no separate genus-`0` construction is needed. -/
347	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
348	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
349	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
350	  (jacobianWitness C).J

352	namespace Jacobian
353	
354	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
355	
356	-- data
357	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
358	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj

361	genus of `C`. -/

364	
365	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
366	instance instIsProper : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom := (jacobianWitness C).proper
367	
368	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
369	instance instGeometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=

/-!
# Smooth morphisms are geometrically reduced

A smooth morphism of schemes is geometrically reduced: every base change to the spectrum of a
field is reduced. Combined with geometric irreducibility, this upgrades the standing hypotheses
of the Jacobian challenge (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom` and
`GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom`) to `GeometricallyIntegral C.hom`, which is what all the
actual geometry of the project consumes.

The commutative-algebra core is that a standard smooth algebra over a domain is reduced. By the
structure theorem for standard smooth algebras (Stacks 00T7,
`RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.exists_etale_mvPolynomial`), such an algebra `S` is étale over a
polynomial ring `P` over the base. Since `S` is flat over the domain `P`, it embeds into
`Frac(P) ⊗[P] S`, which is formally unramified and essentially of finite type over the field
`Frac(P)`, hence reduced by `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field`.

## Main results

* `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain`: a flat, formally unramified algebra,
  essentially of finite type over a domain, is reduced.
* `Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain`, `RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain`,
  `Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain`: étale/standard smooth algebras over
  domains are reduced.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.isReduced_of_field`: a scheme smooth over `Spec` of a field is
  reduced.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyReduced`: a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced
  (instance), together with the `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` variant.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyIntegral`: a smooth, geometrically irreducible
  morphism is geometrically integral (instance), together with the
  `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` variant.

This file is written in mathlib generality and is a candidate for upstreaming.
-/
